Brazil’s National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) has ordered Discord to suspend its "Go Live" feature and all equivalent video streaming tools across the country within three business days.

The platform itself is not blocked. Text chat, voice channels and other core functions remain fully available to Brazilian users. The suspension will stay in place until Discord proves it has implemented effective safeguards to protect children and adolescents.

The decision follows an investigation into child safety failures linked to the death of a 13-year-old girl in Naviraí (Mato Grosso do Sul) on 22 July. Authorities say she was encouraged to take her own life during a roughly 45-minute private Discord livestream. Five teenagers and one 18-year-old have been arrested in connection with the case (Operation Lívia). ANPD cited Discord’s lack of real-time access to livestream content, which prevents automated detection of violations, as well as reliance on flawed systems and user reports.

First Lady Janja da Silva had publicly called for a full ban of the platform days earlier. Discord described the order as "premature," stating it is carefully reviewing the measure, continues to cooperate with law enforcement, and confirmed it quickly removed the private server involved. The company noted that some of the activity was coordinated on other platforms.

Failure to comply could result in fines of up to 50 million reais (approximately $9.7 million) per violation. Discord has 10 business days to appeal. A complete ban of the platform would still require a court decision.
